items.title: Local User System With Bootstrap Admin

requirements.statement: When GitHub-backed automation is enabled, GitHub App mode shall be the preferred integration path over PAT fallback because it offers scoped installation access and repository-aware validation.
If GitHub-backed user sign-in is introduced, it shall resolve to a local user record and preserve the same administrator-versus-member role model used by local authentication.
Email/password and magic-link authentication shall remain available even when GitHub App configuration is absent or invalid.
Setup shall report whether GitHub App mode or PAT fallback is configured and whether repository access is confirmed for the current administrator context.
Provider-login broker configuration shall remain distinct from deployment-local GitHub automation credentials and shall not be reused as the automation credential source.
GitHub automation credentials shall use canonical deployment-local SecretRef names for GitHub App ID, GitHub App private key, GitHub webhook secret, and PAT fallback.
GitHub automation runtime callers shall resolve deployment-local credentials from environment or encrypted SecretRefs without depending on provider-login configuration state.
Broker-issued handoff JWTs shall be verified against broker JWKS material before any local identity linking or session issuance is attempted.
The deployment complete endpoint shall validate signed state and broker handoff JWT before provider-specific identity linking and local session issuance are allowed to proceed.
Broker-issued handoff JWTs shall fail closed when issuer or audience does not match the provider-host configuration.
Broker-issued handoff JWTs shall bind back to the signed deployment state through a matching nonce and provider context.
Successfully validated broker handoff nonces shall be single-use so replay attempts fail closed.
The deployment start endpoint shall redirect to the configured broker start URL with signed state, provider host, and deployment callback URL.
The deployment shall issue a signed provider-auth state token that binds provider, provider host, broker base URL, redirect path, and nonce.
Signed provider-auth state shall expire after a bounded TTL and fail closed when reused after expiry.
Provider-linked identity records shall have durable schema support for authentication metadata such as first and most recent successful authentication timestamps.
External provider identities shall resolve through a local identity record that uniquely maps provider plus host plus provider subject to one local user.
The provider auth foundation shall recognize GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket as the initial provider catalog.
The system shall persist provider-host login configuration including enablement, allowlist posture, and broker trust fields without coupling it to provider automation secrets.
Provider-linked identity records shall store the first and most recent successful provider authentication timestamps.
When no linked identity exists and no existing local user matches by verified provider email, the system shall provision a local user record from provider identity data.
When a provider plus host plus subject identity already exists, the system shall reuse that linked local user instead of creating a second local account.
When no provider identity exists but the provider email is verified and matches an existing local user, the system shall attach the provider identity to that local user.
Provider sign-in shall consume broker-validated provider claims only after the deployment-side state and broker handoff contract has already been validated.
The landing page shall expose a GitHub provider sign-in entrypoint when GitHub.com provider login is enabled.
Local email sign-in and account-creation entrypoints shall remain visible even when provider login is unavailable or disabled.
Successful provider sign-in shall issue the same revocable local browser session credential used by local authentication.
Successful provider sign-in shall resolve to the existing local user model through provider-identity linking before a browser session is issued.
The local session-issuance service for provider sign-in shall remain provider-neutral so additional VCS identity providers can reuse the same token and local-user model.
After successful provider sign-in, the browser shall redirect to the signed deployment redirect path rather than stopping at an intermediate contract response.
Provider login shall evaluate the configured allowlist mode and values before local user linking proceeds.
Provider identities that fail login policy shall be rejected before the system creates or links a local user.
Provider login shall respect per-provider and per-host enablement flags before allowing login resolution.
Allowlist evaluation shall remain provider-neutral so users, organizations, teams, groups, and workspaces can be evaluated through the same policy contract.
New email-backed identities shall support confirmation tracking before they are treated as confirmed accounts.
Authentication shall be anchored to a local user record with a unique email identity.
Local authentication shall support email magic-link sign-in and registration.
Local authentication shall support email-and-password registration and sign-in with password confirmation and minimum-length validation.
Local authentication shall support forgot-password recovery by issuing a reset token and allowing token-based password reset.
The system shall persist session credentials and API keys so they can be listed and revoked as part of account security operations.
The landing page shall present local authentication entrypoints for anonymous users, an enabled provider-login entrypoint when configured, and a sign-out control for authenticated users.
Shared application chrome shall not advertise disabled product areas while baseline mode is active.
Product, setup, RPC, API, and admin route declarations shall remain commented out while baseline mode is active.
The browser route surface shall expose only the landing page and authentication flows, including provider-auth handshake endpoints, while baseline mode is active.
The landing page shall present the copy "Welcome to Jido Code" and explain that the application has been trimmed to a baseline.
The repository shall instruct agents to run bw prime before starting work and use Beadwork for durable local work state.
The repository shall prefer GitHub issues and pull requests for non-trivial collaboration and shall avoid landing changes directly on main.
Auth-provider foundation work shall be specified and implemented inside jido_code rather than split into a separate product repo.
The jido_code repository shall serve as the primary product and implementation repo for active work in this workspace.
The repository shall maintain a package-local .spec workspace for current-truth subject specs, durable ADRs, and generated spec state.
The repository shall include a .spec/AGENTS.md that gives local operating guidance for agents working inside the .spec workspace.
The repository shall include a .spec/decisions/README.md that explains when durable ADRs belong in the workspace.
The repository shall include a .spec/README.md that explains purpose, layout, and workflow.
When planning and verification run, the workspace shall generate .spec/state.json containing indexed subjects, indexed decisions, and verification state.
Administrators shall be able to add users and initiate account creation without reopening unrestricted public registration.
The system shall identify which users are administrators so policy, auditing, and management actions can resolve the acting admin explicitly.
Initial setup shall create or confirm exactly one bootstrap administrator before admin-managed account features are used.
The account model shall treat administrators and standard members as users in one local user system rather than separate identity silos.
Once the bootstrap administrator exists in production, open self-registration shall remain gated unless an administrator explicitly provisions or invites the account.
Both administrators and standard users shall be able to sign in, sign out, and complete forgot-password recovery for their own accounts.

given: GitHub App credentials are configured and the installation can access the expected repositories.
then: The system reports GitHub App mode as ready for the current administrator context.
when: Setup validates GitHub integration.

given: A future GitHub-backed sign-in flow is enabled.
then: The system links that identity to a local user record before authorization decisions are made.
when: A GitHub identity authenticates successfully.

given: GitHub App credentials are not configured and PAT validation succeeds.
then: The system reports PAT fallback readiness without blocking local user authentication flows.
when: Setup validates GitHub integration.

given: A deployment-local GitHub automation secret exists in encrypted SecretRefs.
The same credential is also present in root environment configuration.
then: The root environment value wins and the secret-ref metadata remains non-authoritative for that resolution.
when: GitHub automation resolves that credential.

given: Provider-login configuration is stored in the provider config model.
then: The automation model names deployment-local service secrets separately from provider-login broker fields.
when: GitHub automation service credentials are described for setup and runtime callers.

given: A deployment-local GitHub automation secret is absent from runtime env and present in encrypted SecretRefs under its canonical name.
then: The encrypted SecretRef value is used.
when: GitHub automation resolves that credential.

given: A provider-host config has broker trust fields.
then: Start redirects to the broker contract URL, and complete validates the broker contract before any local provider sign-in work runs.
when: The deployment start and complete endpoints are invoked.

given: A broker returns a signed handoff JWT.
then: Invalid issuer, audience, expiry, or replay attempts fail closed.
when: The deployment validates that JWT against broker trust settings and the signed state nonce.

given: A deployment operator starts provider sign-in for a configured provider host.
then: The provider state round-trips with the same nonce and fails once it expires.
when: The deployment issues and later verifies the provider-auth state token.

given: A local user already exists.
then: Future provider lookups can resolve the same local user through the provider plus host plus subject tuple and keep provider-auth metadata on the identity record.
when: The system records a provider identity for that user.

given: An operator needs to prepare hosted provider login.
then: The system persists provider-neutral login settings without storing automation credentials in the same record.
when: The operator saves provider-host configuration for an approved source provider.

given: No linked provider identity exists and the verified provider email is not yet present in the local directory.
then: The system provisions one local user and future verified identities for the same email attach back to that user.
when: The provider identity authenticates.

given: A provider identity is already linked to a local user.
then: The same local user is returned and the most recent authentication timestamp is refreshed without losing the original first-authenticated timestamp.
when: The same provider identity authenticates again.

given: A local user exists without a provider identity.
then: The provider identity attaches to that local user instead of creating a duplicate user.
when: A provider identity with the same verified email authenticates.

given: GitHub.com provider login has been enabled for the deployment.
then: The page shows both local auth entrypoints and the GitHub sign-in entrypoint.
when: An anonymous visitor opens the landing page.

given: The deployment has already validated broker state and handoff claims for a GitHub identity.
then: The flow links or provisions the local user, issues a revocable session token, and redirects the browser to the signed redirect path.
when: The provider sign-in service consumes those claims.

given: A provider identity does not satisfy the configured allowlist.
then: The identity is rejected before a local user is created or linked.
when: Login is attempted.

given: A provider host is configured with an allowlist.
then: The login is allowed to proceed into local identity linking.
when: Provider identity facts match the configured allowlist values.

given: A provider host is configured but login is disabled.
then: The login is rejected before local user linking begins.
when: A provider identity attempts login.

given: A user prefers passwordless access.
then: The system signs in the existing user or creates the local user identity allowed by policy.
when: The user requests and consumes a valid magic link.

given: A user has forgotten their password.
then: The password is changed and the user can authenticate with the new secret.
when: The user requests reset instructions and completes the reset flow with a valid token.

given: A user has a local email identity and a valid password.
then: The system issues a revocable authenticated session token.
when: The user signs in through the password flow.

given: A bootstrap administrator is signed in.
then: The new account enters the local user system without reopening unrestricted public sign-up.
when: The administrator provisions a new team member account.

given: The deployment has no existing users.
then: The system establishes one bootstrap administrator who becomes the first accountable local user.
when: Initial setup is completed.

given: A standard user account exists in the local directory.
then: The user completes self-service recovery without requiring direct administrator password handling.
when: The user forgets their password.

meta.summary: jido_code authenticates local users with email-backed identities, password and magic-link flows, confirmation, and revocable session credentials.
jido_code exposes only a welcome landing page and authentication flows while the product surface is temporarily trimmed back.
jido_code uses Beadwork for local durable agent state and GitHub issues plus pull requests for shared collaboration.
jido_code keeps local user accounts as the source of truth while supporting GitHub App and PAT integration and preparing for optional GitHub-backed sign-in.
jido_code keeps GitHub automation credentials deployment-local, names them through canonical SecretRefs, and does not reuse provider-login broker configuration for automation.

jido_code is the primary implementation repo, maintains a package-local Spec Led workspace, and evolves auth-provider foundation, linking, login-policy, and GitHub service-credential work inside that repo.
jido_code persists provider-backed user identities and provider login configuration without replacing the local user system.

jido_code signs deployment-owned provider state, validates broker JWT handoffs with issuer and audience trust, blocks nonce replay, and enforces the contract that must pass before provider-specific local sign-in can proceed.
jido_code resolves provider identities to local users by reusing an existing identity, linking verified email addresses, or provisioning a new local user when needed.

jido_code exposes a GitHub provider sign-in entrypoint, consumes broker-validated provider claims, links them to the local user system, and issues the same revocable local session tokens used by email sign-in.
jido_code evaluates provider login enablement and provider-neutral allowlists before allowing provider identities to resolve into local users.
Canonical workspace contract for authored specs and generated Spec Led state.
jido_code boots with an initial administrator and grows into an admin-managed multi-user account system.
